To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Stl repressors of SaPIs bind dUTPases of helper phage and that the dNTPase activity is strongly inhibited by this interaction.

the transfer of phage-related mobile pathogenicity islands is controlled by dUTPases that inhibit the binding of a repressor protein to the cognate DNA and that dUTPases are also involved in the regulation of the transfer of other phage-related mobile elements.

the transfer of phage-related mobile genetic elements of the pathogen Staphylococus aureus is controlled by the dUTP:Stl protein complex, which inhibits dUTPase activity and thereby prevents the sanitizing of the dNTP pools.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of dUTPase action and reveals a novel function for this ubiquitous enzyme.
the molecular mechanism by which a phage-encoded enzyme controls gene expression and the fate of its host genome.
the novel role of bacterial dUTPases as repressors of gene expression and reveals a novel mechanism of dUTPase action in bacterial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dUTPAse: Stl complex is a novel molecular mechanism for the control of SaPI gene expression and that the dUtpase is a novel regulator of SaPI transfer.
dUTPases are not only enzymes but also potent regulators of the dNTP pools.
the dUTPAse:Stl complex is a novel mechanism of gene expression control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dUTPs are not merely a source of UMP but they also play an important role in gene expression control.
the dUTPage is a novel repressor protein that controls gene expression in the presence of dUTP.
dUTPases are not only involved in DNA repair and replication, but can also be used as regulatory proteins to modulate the expression of genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a bacterial repressor is inhibited by a viral enzyme and that the inhibition is mediated by the enzyme substrate, dUTP.
dUTPases, which are ubiquitous and highly conserved enzymes, can act as regulators of gene expression.
dUTPases, in addition to their established role in genome stability, can be used to control gene expression.
